intro: Conjunctional adverbs are the words that join sentences without changing word order the way weil and obwohl do: they take position 1 (or a middle-field slot) and the verb follows at 2. They come in families. Concession: trotzdem, dennoch (nevertheless), allerdings, jedoch (however — jedoch can also sit inside the sentence). Consequence: deshalb, deswegen, daher, folglich, dadurch (as a result), also (so). Addition: außerdem, zudem, darüber hinaus (moreover). Alternative: sonst (otherwise), stattdessen (instead). Contrast: dagegen, hingegen (by contrast). Time: dann, danach, inzwischen, schließlich. Each family also has a subordinating twin (obwohl, weil, während, wenn nicht) — and choosing between the two grammars is what makes your prose flow rather than stack. Connectors are the visible structure of any text you write: a reader follows your argument by them.
tips[0].title: Position 1, verb at 2 — or in the middle
tips[0].text: Es war teuer. Trotzdem haben wir es gekauft. = Es war teuer, wir haben es trotzdem gekauft. Both orders are correct; the fronted one stresses the link.
tips[0].trap: 'Trotzdem wir haben …' is English order ('nevertheless we have'). After a fronted connector the verb comes immediately.
tips[0].check.why: A fronted connector takes position 1, so the verb follows immediately in position 2, before the subject.
tips[1].title: The families and their subordinate twins
tips[1].text: trotzdem / dennoch / allerdings / jedoch ↔ obwohl · deshalb / daher / folglich / deswegen ↔ weil · außerdem / zudem ↔ (und) · sonst ↔ wenn … nicht · stattdessen ↔ (an)statt dass · dagegen / hingegen ↔ während (contrast).
tips[1].check.why: The verb war stands at the end of the first clause, so you need the subordinating twin obwohl; after trotzdem the verb would come straight next.
tips[2].title: Register: which one when
tips[2].text: Speech: trotzdem, deshalb, außerdem, sonst. Writing: dennoch, daher, folglich, zudem, allerdings, hingegen. Both are correct everywhere; the written ones signal a careful, formal register.
tips[2].check.why: folglich, like daher, is the written choice for a consequence; deswegen and also are the everyday spoken ones.
tips[3].title: sonst = or else; stattdessen = instead
tips[3].text: Beeil dich, sonst verpassen wir den Zug (or else). Er kam nicht; stattdessen schickte er eine Nachricht (instead). Two small ones that carry a lot.
tips[3].check.why: sonst means 'or else': it names what happens if you don't do the first thing. stattdessen means 'instead'.
remember[0]: Connector at 1, verb at 2: trotzdem haben wir …
remember[2]: Within a family any member is correct — the quiz accepts trotzdem / dennoch, deshalb / daher / folglich, außerdem / zudem alike.

hook: Link your sentences with trotzdem, deshalb, außerdem and sonst so a reader can follow your argument step by step.
